IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL NOS.75-76 OF 2025  (Arising out of SLP(Criminal) No.10317-10318 of 2024)
 AMIT KUMAR CHAUDHARY ...APPELL  VERSUS  THE STATE OF BIHAR & ANR. ...RESPON  O R D E R 1.
Leave granted.

2. The present appeals are filed challenging the orders dated 16.05.2023 and 15.12.2023 passed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court in Cr. Misc. No.62411 of 2022 and in Criminal Misc.
No.72655 of 2023, rejecting the application of the appellant seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with Complaint Case No.175 of 2022, dated 29.03.2022, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 379, 323, 504, 506/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. This Court vide the order dated 31.07.2024 had granted interim protection to the appellant, which has continued till this date.

4. The learned counsel for the appellant states that the RAVI ARORA appellant shall remain present before the concerned Court as and when called and shall abide by any condition that may be imposed by the Trial Court.
5. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, we are inclined to accept the present appeals.

Hence, it is directed that in the event of arrest of the appellant in connection with Complaint Case No.175 of 2022, dated 29.03.2022, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 379, 323, 504, 506/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibiton Act, he shall be released on bail on the terms and conditions that may be imposed by the Amit Kumar Chaudhary vs The State Of Bihar on 6 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101643035/

6. It goes without saying that any breach of the conditions that may be imposed by the Trial Court for releasing him on bail, shall entail cancellation of the bail.
7. Subject to the afore-stated, the present appeals are allowed.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
